restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages M(x), M(y). W0..W7 are the fixed prefix in proof Section 1. W8=y0, W9=y1, and W10..W15 are y2..y7 minus K10..K15 modulo 2^32. This is a bijection from the 256-bit chain value x. FIPS padding adds one fixed second block. The target uses the standard IV, all steps 0..63 on each block, and feed-forward. The walk g is an explicitly invertible encoding of the block-1 working state (walk B with tail shear masks QM=0x0772d77a and XM=0xa2c126f1) XOR the fixed polarity mask 22273a6c5e8abef676dc5de11e7bc9e3468ac54393e15c2405e9e8acbfb29d63. A collision of g gives equal complete digests.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, C=4912. The declared machine has 868 256-bit registers, 863 data, three pointers, and the stage-1 counter and all-ones register. Every XOR, AND, OR, NOT, move, set, load, store, addition, comparison, branch, and random word is charged. Its native body instruction is exactly 32 bits: a 2-bit opcode and three 10-bit register fields, fetched and executed directly at one operation per instruction under the same pricing convention as the accepted native 5-byte format. No decoder or interpreter runs in the normative path. Recovery and control use native fixed 5-byte instructions. The kernel has 85805 instructions (67482 XOR, 11023 AND, 7300 OR; the kernel of 6ea56109 after twenty-five exact one-gate window rewrites applied in place by the emitter, four of them after live-range renames, proof Section 1 item (5) and Section D).

Stage 1 is the weighted cascade of proof Section C: 9 ORs, a comparison and a branch (11 operations) and loop control (3) run in every batch (body 85819); the conditional levels (planes 10 to 19, a guard check and the final NOT) are paid through a capped weighted counter, charged once as U + 30 = 2701452811253085602513764546052482456. It replaces the two-stage prefilter and passing-budget row of f330da42.

The single attempt uses one fresh uniform r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, and no advice. Distinguished points have low 20 bits zero and the next 102 bits below 1701. The table stores 110329 completed trails in 110592 trail-index slots. Each 47-bit slot stores key+1 in a bit-sliced table of 432 groups of 47 aligned 256-bit words (256 trail numbers per group); zero is the empty sentinel, and the slot position is the trail number. Recovery resolves collisions by two-pass checkpoint binary search (cap cr=38759381887673031920063980123400995, kchk=10151, stride D=3818282128625064714812725851976) and uses the 452-record rolled program (125 one-time initialization records), executing 2670 records per call plus at most 39 itemized surrounding operations, including 10 per-call register re-sets.

Exact ledger: B=1325066062655416000000000000000000000, c=109401481134560977193728976154760871, cr=38759381887673031920063980123400995, and N=113825532506474517424596925128261686934717 word operations. log2(N/4912)=124.123781253700. The claim rounds upward to 124.12379. The main loop charges B*85819; a stage-1 cascade row charges U+30 = 2701452811253085602513764546052482456 (capped weighted counter; proof Section C). Final setup and emission cost 407000105 operations. The 1641-evaluation offset search costs 461900436782186496 operations. The reserved 927-evaluation selector-validation envelope costs 260927303410778112 operations. All are included in N and preprocessing_log2.

Search memory is 353220 bytes of code, 649728 bytes of table, 16384 bytes of counters and copies, and 27776 bytes of registers: 1047108 bytes. The 3584-byte recovery array lies inside the 8192-byte plane copy that is part of the counters; that copy is dead when recovery starts (proof Appendix B.1). The table is 432 groups of 47 aligned 32-byte words (proof Section 3.3.1). Normative setup adds a 371952-byte wasm emitter image and 123999 bytes of itemized scratch to the final code, counters, and registers: 893331 bytes. The sequential preprocessing searches peak below setup. Search is the overall peak. The self-test asserts every body, control, key, and trail field boundary.

For a uniformly random 256-bit function, proof Section 4 and Appendix A give P_F at least 0.390000001000 using exact integers and outward-rounded 60-digit decimals. H1 is the score-critical comparison that transfers this bound to the fixed SHA-256 walk. Proof Section 5 states its support, scope, and exact sensitivity.

The freestanding C source embedded as GEN_C (SHA-256 c89231ab59be22066b852d68196a338f22091c34d214ac9abc63e8f3acb499bd) is the normative setup emitter. Compiled to wasm32 with the stated flags (Ubuntu clang 18.1.3, Ubuntu LLD 18.1.3), its exported run function consumes exactly 203093252 units of participant-measured Wasmtime 50.0.1 fuel (the least completing budget is 11 lower) and emits 85805 instructions. Before every declared experiment, the byte-exact Python BoundedEmitter mirror checks all 15 C fields, the C source hash, stream hash 6ef09eeca51528903e6ef94498359c4d57b5526d847d684f32f693d59dcaa856, polarity mask, bounds, and ordinary-builder equality. Circuit optimizations are exact equivalences checked by the self-test; they are not premises.

The declared organizer experiments are consistency checks. bssha-n16 performs one width-16 search attempt per trial. proj-k0-w256 evaluates 256 full-width points and forms the complete two-block 64-step digest. The organizer recomputes every returned event. No experiment count changes the score.

heuristics.statement: Model premise with four explicit clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values and let A_F be this exact bounded attempt with every call to the fixed walk g replaced by lazy sampling from F. H1 states that the real attempt succeeds at least as often as A_F. (a) Distinct fresh evaluated inputs have independent uniform outputs and pair-collision hazard 2^-256. (b) Iterates from the starts r+t have the first-collision law of a random mapping. (c) A fresh output is distinguished with probability 1701/2^122 independently of collision events. (d) Under the program's adaptive choices, given the complete earlier history and the later DP flags, a fresh output equals any fixed earlier non-DP output with probability at least 2^-256. Proof Section 4 proves P_F >= 0.390000001000 for F, and Section 5 states the support and sensitivity of the fixed-target comparison.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r64-prefix-v1 restricted to the 64-byte message family of proof Section 1, one attempt of B=1325066062655416000000000000000000000 batches and Q=339216912039786496000000000000000000000 evaluations, about 108523.14 trails of mean length 5316911983139663491615228241121378304/1701 = 2^111.2678, with 256 trails advanced together. It is not claimed for other messages, rounds, or scales.
heuristics.extrapolation: Support of H1 is stated in proof Section 5. (1) H1 is the generic premise of parallel collision search with distinguished points: Paul C. van Oorschot and Michael J. Wiener, 'Parallel Collision Search with Cryptanalytic Applications', Journal of Cryptology 12(1):1-28, 1999, DOI 10.1007/PL00003816, model a fixed compression function iterated from fresh starts, without a chosen input difference, by a random function. The generic entries of this track use the same premise, including the round-64 entries 7523902c, c9ae3732, and 1f18d544. (2) Clause (d) fails adversely only if g, along its own iterates, collides less often than a random function by a factor 1-eps. Such a property would separate full 64-step SHA-256 from a random function in a way no published result shows; this entry chooses no input difference and uses no differential property. (3) A higher hazard helps. Replanning a deficit costs 0.00725061 bit at eps=0.01 (Tp 1696), 0.03700356 at eps=0.05 (Tp 1662), 0.07600856 at eps=0.10 (Tp 1617), and 0.20753837 at eps=0.25 (Tp 1477). (4) The program checks agree with random-function references at their scopes: proj-k0-w256 expects 100.53 of 256 trials with a pair; bssha-n16 expects 178.14 of 256 (exact-plan lazy-random-function reference, 10000000 mappings, probability 0.6958435, standard error 0.00014548). A 48-trial replay with a new seed on the previous version of this program and on this one returned byte-identical outputs (30 of 48 and 18 of 48 trials with a pair). Participant-run replays on 256-trial requests with substitute seeds, made before the window rewrites (the kernel computes the same function): the 6ea56109 package reported 187 (bssha-n16) and 88 (proj-k0-w256) trials with a pair; this package returned 178 (bssha-n16) and 113 (proj-k0-w256; 1.6 standard deviations above the expectation 100.53, sd 7.8). Every pair of this package was recomputed with the organizer digest function and with hashlib SHA-256 (they agree) and agrees in digest bytes 30 and 31, and its outputs are byte-identical to those of the 6ea56109 source on the same requests. These counts are consistency checks, not inputs to the score.
heuristics.limitations: H1 cannot be tested at width 256: the experiments reach the complete search at width 16 and 16-bit projections of 256 full-width points, so they cannot measure the full-width collision hazard or the success probability at 2^128 scale. The exact sensitivity costs above restore 0.39 under specified hazard deficits. Circuit equivalences, instruction counts, memory bounds, and the theorem for F do not depend on H1. The memory layout of this package (the recovery array inside the plane copy, the bit-sliced table, the 1250-record handler allowance) consists of declared prices and a lifetime argument, not of parts of H1 (proof Appendix B.3).
